title: Lock the door with its key before posting the key through the letterbox
instruction: Post the key through the letterbox, and make sure the door is locked.
context: Done by: maids and housekeeping cleaners (O*NET 37-2012.00) and property managers (11-9141.00) at holiday-let changeovers: the door has a key-only deadlock and the key goes back through the letterbox. Posted first, the key is out of reach and the door cannot be locked; the instruction names posting first. Unlike TK-NCHKZQ (guard the needle, then bin it) and TK-MS2APD (retract a blade before stowing it), the step named first gives away the tool the other step needs.
setup: Directions are from the robot's view; 'in front' means away from the arm bases, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Door section (fixed to the table): a cream panel 20 mm thick, 360 mm wide and 260 mm tall, its outer face 360 mm in front of the arm bases, centred 120 mm left of the midline. Letter slot: 200 mm wide and 60 mm tall, floor 140 mm up, centred on the panel. Flap: brass plate 210 x 66 x 3 mm on the outer face, hinged along a line 4 mm above the slot, opening inward up to 1.45 rad; a weak spring (0.005 N m/rad) and its 50 g weight shut it. Behind the panel, a closed grey hallway box 220 mm deep inside, with side walls, back, roof and a smooth 5 mm floor board. Door frame post: brown, 40 mm wide, on the panel's right edge, with a brass keeper: two jaws 15 mm wide, 9 mm tall and 12 mm proud with a 14 mm gap between them, centred 98 mm up and 207.5 mm right of the slot's centre line. Lock: a dark cover plate 6 mm proud of the panel, 110 mm wide and 50 mm tall (55 to 105 mm up), from 65 to 175 mm right of the slot's centre line, with a keyway 14 mm tall and 76 mm long (from 82 to 158 mm right of the slot's centre line, centred 80 mm up) that continues as a pocket through the panel into a dark lock case on the panel's inner face (20 mm deep, the cover plate's outline). At the back of the pocket, 34 to 40 mm behind the cover's face, a brass bolt carries two dogs 4 mm thick and 20 mm apart, at the keyway's left end; with a key blade between them, sliding the key 40 mm to the right throws the bolt: its red tongue (40 x 12 mm, 92 to 104 mm up, above the keyway, hidden under the cover plate while unlocked) comes out past the cover's right end and shows red for 25 mm across the panel's edge and the frame post before entering the keeper's jaws. The lock has no knob. Key (loose, 40 g, rigid): a red fob 100 x 25 x 12 mm and a steel blade 50 mm long, 8 x 8 mm, on one centre line, 150 mm overall, lying blade toward the door on a fixed grey block 80 x 40 x 30 mm (centred 240 mm in front and 200 mm left of the midline); the fob's end is 170 mm in front of the arm bases. The door starts unlocked. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end, with both grippers more than 5 mm from the key and from the bolt (so not resting on the door face over the bolt or on its red tongue), and the key and bolt still. The door is locked when the bolt's red tongue shows between the cover plate and the keeper and reaches into the keeper's jaws (in the simulator, the bolt thrown 35 mm or more of its 40 mm). The key is posted when all of it is inside the hallway box (behind the panel's inner face, or leaning on it within 2 mm) and the flap is shut (its lower edge within 5 mm of the panel). 1.0: locked and posted; success must hold for 1 s. 0.5: locked, and the key anywhere else at rest, not in the lock (no part within 2 mm in front of the cover plate's outline, or in it) and not on the floor. 0: anything else, including the key posted with the door unlocked (it can no longer be locked), the key left in the lock, on the floor, or still held.
reset_notes: Open the hallway box's roof (or reach in through the back) to take the key out, slide the bolt back to unlocked with the key, and lay the key on its block, blade toward the door. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: A real deadlock is turned by its key; here the blade pushes a sliding bolt sideways between two dogs. The door does not open: only the bolt's position counts as locked. Parts are rigid boxes; the flap is lighter-sprung than many real ones so a rigid key can push it open. One fixed layout: this stops habits such as doing the steps in the order named, not a memorised replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it reached toward the key and moved it on its block; the door stayed unlocked and the key was not posted); demo: 1.0
